Subject: Post-call recap — Helix decision criteria and next steps

Hi Priya — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call highlights: 
- Primary use case: low-latency retrieval-augmented generation for clinician-facing UI (single-turn queries, heavy concurrency). 
- Deployment preference: Helix prefers Dedicated capacity but asked about Private (VPC) if we need to meet internal networking / data residency policies. 
- Decision criteria called out on the call: latency (p95 target), cost per 1M tokens, SLA for uptime and failover, and security evidence (SOC 2 + network architecture). 
- Stakeholder map we captured: 
  - Economic buyer / budget owner: Dana Lopez (CFO) — not on this thread yet. 
  - Product/ML sponsor: Priya Shah (you). 
  - Security reviewer: Elaine Park (CISO). 
  - Procurement: procurement@helixanalytics.com (TBD contact). 

Open clarifications we promised to confirm: 
1) Latency target: you mentioned p95 under ~60ms for 1-2k concurrent users — can you confirm if 60ms p95 is the hard target or if 100ms p95 is acceptable for initial rollout? 
2) Cost guardrails: is there an internal guideline (e.g., <$X per 1M tokens) or a target monthly run-rate we should optimize for? 
3) Timeline & procurement: you mentioned a preferred decision by end of Q3 and an initial 4-week PoC. Is that still the plan and who owns procurement sign-off? 

Action items I’m proposing: 
- I’ll send an estimate (Dedicated vs Private scenarios) plus SOC2 and our standard SLA summary by EOD tomorrow. (Attachments: pricing + security checklist.) 
- Marissa (solutions) to propose a PoC plan & acceptance criteria. 
- Sergio (legal) to flag any typical commercial terms we should expect to negotiate. 

Can you confirm the latency target and procurement owner so I can tailor the estimate? Also, is it OK to include Dana and Elaine on follow-ups?

Thanks — Jonas

--

Thanks Jonas — helpful write-up. Confirming a few items from our side: 

1) Latency: our product team would like p95 <= 60ms for the clinician UI for the GA rollout. For the initial internal PoC we can accept up to 90-100ms while we iterate, but the purchase decision will require a clear plan to get to <= 60ms. 
2) Cost: our finance team is targeting an annual TCO that keeps per-1M token costs below $0.50 (we understand this is broad — please provide scenarios). 
3) SLA: we need a formal SLA; target is 99.9% uptime with defined credits. If you have a standard SLA doc, please include. 
4) Timeline & procurement: CFO Dana Lopez is the final approver for any committed spend. I’ll loop Dana in on the next update. Procurement contact is procurement@helixanalytics.com — I’ll introduce them after I share your materials internally. 

PoC: 3–4 week PoC sounds right. Key acceptance criteria for us: (a) sustained p95 < 90ms at 1k concurrent simulated users, (b) accuracy regression <= 2% vs our baseline prompts, (c) integration via your SDK + VPC connectivity for private deployment test. 

Can you also send SOC 2 Type II attestation and a short note on how you handle key management and data retention? Elaine is CC’d for security specifics.

Best,
Priya
Product Lead, Helix Analytics
priya@helixanalytics.com

Jonas / Priya — attaching the initial pricing pack and our security checklist for Helix (see attachments). Summary below: 

Attachment highlights: 
- redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf: two commercial scenarios (monthly reserved pool commit vs on-demand burst) with projected p95 latency estimates at 1k concurrent for the recommended model family. 
- redwood-soc2-type2-attestation.pdf: our latest SOC 2 Type II attestation and summary of controls. 
- helix-security-checklist.xlsx: a quick mapping of Helix questions (KMS, network peering, retention) to our answers and docs. 

Notes on tradeoffs: 
- Dedicated gives the most predictable p95 behavior and simpler SLA guarantees; Private (VPC) adds network setup time and may increase tail latency slightly depending on peering/topology. We included both in the packet. 
- Initial PoC: recommend a 3-week focused test — week 1 baseline and infra setup, week 2 load testing and tuning, week 3 integration and acceptance. We include measurable acceptance criteria aligned with Priya’s list. 

Next steps: 
- Jonas: share the packet with Dana and procurement once you have the intro.
- Priya: confirm whether to proceed with Dedicated PoC or run VPC test first. 

If helpful we can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff tomorrow to run through the PoC plan and test harness.

Thanks,
Marissa
